chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Shami, from al-Husayn ibn Hanzala, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the effect of gourd on the mind?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi highlights the cognitive benefits of consuming gourd (al-dubba'), reflecting the Shia tradition of linking dietary habits to intellectual enhancement. It underscores the holistic view of health in Imami scholarship, where physical nourishment is seen as directly supporting spiritual and mental clarity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad,f rom Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Shamy, from Al Husayn Bin Hanzala, from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws) having said:
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Shamiy from al-Husayn ibn Hanzalah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
Gourd, squash increases al-Damagh (abilities of the brain).”’
